claims.text: Compositionally complex or high-entropy alloys can be used to produce a ductile–brittle–ductile transition.
The initial material state consists of conventional alloys.
Conventional alloys should be replaced with compositionally complex or high-entropy alloys.
The relevant behavior occurs within a narrow temperature window.
Alloy composition is the structural mediator connecting material replacement to the predicted behavior.
Temper-embrittlement resistance is the operative mechanism in compositionally complex or high-entropy alloys.
The predicted outcome is a ductile–brittle–ductile transition.
Conventional alloys exhibiting temper embrittlement constitute the baseline.
The hypothesis is bounded to the temperature range in which temper embrittlement occurs.
There is a lack of specific evidence concerning ductile–brittle–ductile behavior in compositionally complex or high-entropy alloys.
Observation of temper embrittlement in a compositionally complex or high-entropy alloy within a narrow temperature window would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: Temper-embrittlement resistance would tend to suppress the brittle regime, whereas the predicted ductile–brittle–ductile outcome requires an intervening brittle regime; no alternative cause of that regime is supplied.

The hypothesis predicts a brittle interval but declares temper embrittlement within a narrow temperature interval to be falsifying. It does not distinguish the predicted brittle interval from the allegedly falsifying embrittlement.
